title: Delicious Smoked Cheese Dishes Using a Reusable Grill Mat
meta_description: Discover tasty smoked cheese grill mat recipes that turn your BBQ Grill Mats into a flavor powerhouse. Easy, non‑stick dishes for any grill enthusiast.
html:
When you pull out a reusable grill mat, the first thing that comes to mind is usually veggies or fish. But the real magic happens when you pair a mat with smoked cheese. Using BBQ Grill Mats, you can create a series of smoked cheese grill mat recipes that stay perfectly melted, develop a subtle char, and never stick to the grates.

Why a Grill Mat Is Perfect for Smoked Cheese

A non‑stick, heat‑resistant mat creates a gentle barrier between the cheese and the hot grill. That means:

  • No flare‑ups – the cheese can melt without dripping into the fire.
  • Even heat distribution – the cheese softens uniformly, giving a creamy interior and a lightly browned top.
  • Easy cleanup – the reusable BBQ Grill Mats wipe clean with a quick rinse, so you spend more time eating and less time scrubbing.

Because the mat stays flat, you can stack toppings, fold the cheese, or even grill a whole wheel without worrying about it sliding off.

Smoked Cheese Grilled Quesadilla – A Quick Lunch Fix

This is the ultimate "cheese‑pull" dish, and it works beautifully on a grill mat. You’ll need:

  1. 2 large flour tortillas
  2. 1 cup smoked cheddar, grated
  3. ½ cup shredded Monterey Jack
  4. 1 tbsp butter, softened
  5. Optional: sliced jalapeños, cilantro, or a drizzle of chipotle mayo

Spread butter on the outer side of each tortilla. Sprinkle the smoked cheeses evenly over one tortilla, add any extra toppings, then top with the second tortilla, butter side up. Place the assembled quesadilla on a pre‑heated BBQ Grill Mat, close the lid, and cook for 3‑4 minutes per side. The mat prevents the cheese from seeping through the grates, giving you a perfectly crisp exterior and a molten, smoky center.

Smoked Cheese & Apple Grilled Panini – Sweet Meets Savory

For a brunch twist, try this panini. The key is the mat’s ability to hold thin slices of cheese and fruit together without tearing the bread.

Ingredients:

  • 2 slices sourdough bread
  • 2 tbsp grainy mustard
  • 4 thin slices smoked Gouda
  • ½ thinly sliced Granny Smith apple
  • 1 tsp butter, melted

Spread mustard on the bread, layer Gouda and apple, then close the sandwich. Lightly brush the outside with melted butter. Place the sandwich on a BBQ Grill Mat over medium heat, press down with a grill press or heavy skillet, and grill for 2‑3 minutes per side. The cheese melts into the apple’s tartness, and the mat keeps everything from slipping into the flames.

Smoked Cheese-Stuffed Portobello Burgers – A Hearty Vegetarian Option

Portobello caps are the perfect vessel for a cheese‑filled burger. Using a grill mat ensures the cheese stays inside while the caps develop a beautiful char.

Steps:

  1. Clean 4 large portobello caps, remove stems, and brush with olive oil.
  2. Mix 1 cup smoked mozzarella with ¼ cup chopped fresh basil, salt, and pepper.
  3. Spoon the cheese mixture into each cap, pressing lightly to fill.
  4. Lay the caps on a pre‑heated BBQ Grill Mat, gill‑side down, and close the lid.
  5. Cook 5‑6 minutes, until the caps are tender and the cheese is bubbly.

Serve on a bun with lettuce, tomato, and a smear of garlic aioli. The mat’s non‑stick surface means the cheese never drips onto the coals, preventing bitterness and keeping the grill clean.

Smoked Cheese Breakfast Pizza – A Morning Game‑Changer

Who says pizza is only for dinner? A quick breakfast pizza on a grill mat can be ready in under ten minutes.

Ingredients:

  • Pre‑made pizza dough (or flatbread)
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • ½ cup smoked provolone, shredded
  • 2 eggs
  • Fresh chives, salt, pepper

Brush the dough with olive oil and place it on the BBQ Grill Mats. Sprinkle the smoked provolone, then crack two eggs onto the cheese. Close the lid and grill for 4‑5 minutes, until the crust is golden and the eggs are set to your liking. The mat keeps the cheese from sliding off and catches any egg whites that might otherwise fall through the grates.

Tips for Mastering Smoked Cheese Grill Mat Recipes

Even with a great product like BBQ Grill Mats, a few tricks can elevate your results:

  • Pre‑heat the mat: Give the mat a minute on the grill before adding food. This prevents the cheese from sticking as it hits a warm surface.
  • Control the heat: Medium‑high works for most cheese dishes. Too high and the cheese may burn before it fully melts.
  • Use a gentle press: For sandwiches and paninis, a light press helps the cheese melt evenly without crushing the bread.
  • Clean while warm: After grilling, let the mat cool just enough to handle, then wipe it with a damp cloth. No scrubbing needed.

With these guidelines, you’ll find that smoked cheese grill mat recipes become a staple in your grilling repertoire.

FAQ

Can I use the BBQ Grill Mats on a gas, charcoal, or electric grill?

Yes. The mats are heat‑resistant up to 500°F and work on any grill type, making them versatile for indoor or outdoor cooking.

Do the mats affect the smoky flavor of the cheese?

The mat itself is neutral, but because it prevents flare‑ups, the cheese absorbs a clean, consistent smoke without the bitter notes that come from burnt drippings.

How do I clean the grill mat after cooking with cheese?

Let the mat cool, wipe it with a damp sponge, and if needed, a mild dish soap. Rinse and air‑dry. The non‑stick surface resists residue, so a quick wipe is usually enough.
